LanguageData.NoTableNeeded.Settings.NotScanned: The food scan has not run yet. Restart RimWorld with No Table Needed enabled.
LanguageData.NoTableNeeded.Settings.Summary:
{0} of {1} foods no longer ask for a table.
Everything else — simple, fine and lavish meals, nutrient paste, baby food — is untouched, and eating one off the ground still costs mood.
LanguageData.NoTableNeeded.Settings.NotAMeal: Food that is not a meal
LanguageData.NoTableNeeded.Settings.NotAMealTip: Anything the game ranks below a terrible meal: raw produce, eggs, fish, milk, chocolate, ambrosia, kibble, raw meat. The game already refuses to treat these as meals in every other respect — a colonist eating one gets "ate raw food" and knows perfectly well it was not dinner.
LanguageData.NoTableNeeded.Settings.PreservedRationsT: Meals that keep for {0} days or more, or never rot at all: pemmican, packaged survival meals, insect jelly. Keeping is the whole point of these foods, and what they keep for is being eaten away from home. Cooked meals rot in 4 days and are not affected.
LanguageData.NoTableNeeded.Settings.WhenHungryTip: A colonist who has not eaten in far too long does not complain about the furniture. Past the threshold below, the penalty is skipped whatever the food was, lavish meal included. Hunger is read at the end of the meal but before it is swallowed, so it is the hunger they walked in with.
LanguageData.NoTableNeeded.Settings.HungerThresholdTi: Urgently hungry is the recommended setting. Colonists start looking for food while merely hungry, so forgiving from "hungry" would drop the penalty on nearly every meal; from "urgently hungry" it only forgives the meals that came too late — caravans, sieges, famine, a neglected prisoner. Starving is stricter still.
